record.paper_title: The Hidden Subgroup Problem - Review and Open Problems
record.original_question: For which finite groups can the information-theoretic ability to distinguish hidden subgroups with only polynomially many oracle queries be converted into a full polynomial-time quantum algorithm that actually outputs subgroup generators, rather than requiring exponential classical postprocessing?

evidence.quote: However, this reconstruction is harder in the nonabelian case. For example, Ettinger, Høyer, and Knill [46] have shown only polynomially many calls in log |G| to the oracle distinguishes subgroups for any group G information theoretically, but it is currently unknown how to extract generators for H without exponential classical postprocessing time.
Unfortunately, deducing H from the resulting quantum state requires exponential classical time, and it is still open for which groups this can be reduced to a polynomial time quantum algorithm.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Let $G$ be a finite group and let $f : G \to S$ be a function on $G$ taking values in some finite set $S$. We say that $f$ hides a subgroup $H \le G$ if $f$ is constant on each left coset of $H$ and takes distinct values on distinct cosets. The Hidden Subgroup Problem (HSP) for $G$ is: given oracle access to such an $f$, output a set of generators for the hidden subgroup $H$.

It is known (Ettinger–Høyer–Knill) that for every finite group $G$, only $\mathrm{poly}(\log|G|)$ quantum queries to the oracle suffice to determine $H$ information-theoretically: the resulting quantum state (or measurement statistics) contains enough information to identify $H$ uniquely. However, the only general procedure known for extracting generators of $H$ from this information uses classical postprocessing time exponential in $\log|G|$.

Problem. Characterize the families of finite groups $G$ for which the information-theoretic identifiability of $H$ from polynomially many quantum oracle queries can be upgraded to a fully efficient (i.e. $\mathrm{poly}(\log|G|)$-time) quantum algorithm that outputs generators of the hidden subgroup $H$. In particular, determine for which classes of nonabelian groups such a polynomial-time quantum algorithm exists, and identify obstructions for the remaining classes.
artifact.status_search_result: The general nonabelian Hidden Subgroup Problem remains open. Polynomial-time quantum algorithms are known only for special classes such as abelian groups, normal hidden subgroups, nil-2 groups, extraspecial groups, and certain semidirect products. No general efficient procedure for converting the information-theoretic identifiability (Ettinger–Høyer–Knill) into polynomial-time generator extraction is known, and important cases such as the symmetric and dihedral groups (linked to graph isomorphism and lattice problems respectively) remain unresolved as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Hidden subgroup problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The nonabelian case remains open; an efficient solution would give rise to an efficient quantum algorithm for graph isomorphism.
status_evidence.claim: General nonabelian HSP is still open.

status_evidence.title: An Efficient Quantum Algorithm for the Hidden Subgroup Problem in Extraspecial Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Polynomial time quantum algorithms have been developed for finding hidden subgroups in extraspecial groups.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists for specific nonabelian group classes.

status_evidence.title: Efficient quantum algorithms for some instances of the non-Abelian HSP
status_evidence.snippet: Efficient quantum algorithms for some instances of the non-Abelian hidden subgroup problem.
status_evidence.claim: Only specific nonabelian instances are known to admit efficient quantum algorithms.
